title: Many-body ergodicity breaking from wavefunction snapshots
authors: Riccardo Andreoni, Devendra Singh Bhakuni, Marcello Dalmonte, Lev Vidmar, Miroslav Hopjan
abstract: Modern quantum experiments can probe many-body wavefunctions through projective measurements, providing snapshots of individual many-body configurations. A fundamental question is whether the intrinsic structure of their measurement distributions can reveal quantum dynamics beyond predefined observables. Here, we address this question at the many-body ergodicity-breaking transition using two complementary characteristics of nonequilibrium wavefunction snapshots: their binary intrinsic dimension (BID) and the topology of wavefunction networks constructed from Hamming distances. We show that the critical point is characterized by an extensive but submaximal BID, and scale-free network connectivity with highly connected hubs. These signatures distinguish the ergodic, critical, and nonergodic regimes, and provide experimentally accessible probes of ergodicity breaking from projective measurement snapshots.
summary: This work proposes using statistical measures like Binary Intrinsic Dimension (BID) and network analysis on wavefunction snapshots to diagnose quantum dynamics. By analyzing the quantum sun model, the authors show that the ergodicity-breaking transition is marked by specific, measurable changes in these intrinsic data structures. This offers a powerful, non-observable-specific tool for quantum simulation experiments.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the intrinsic structure of projective measurement distributions (wavefunction snapshots) can reveal quantum dynamics beyond predefined observables, specifically focusing on the many-body ergodicity-breaking transition.
main_result: The critical point is uniquely characterized by a combination of extensive but submaximal Binary Intrinsic Dimension (BID) and scale-free network connectivity with highly connected hubs, distinguishing it from ergodic and nonergodic regimes.
method: The authors employ data-driven diagnostics, including calculating the Binary Intrinsic Dimension (BID) from pairwise Hamming distances and constructing wavefunction networks based on these distances.
model_or_system: The analysis uses the quantum sun model, a paradigmatic toy model for studying the many-body ergodicity-breaking transition, involving coupled qubits governed by a specific Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Binary Intrinsic Dimension (BID), network connectivity (scale-free vs. random), and the system's ergodic state.
important_parameters: The coupling strength $\alpha$, which controls the transition; the critical point $\alpha_c \approx 0.75$.
main_assumptions: The number of collected snapshots ($N_s$) is much smaller than the full Hilbert-space dimension ($N_s \ll D$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the sampling of many-body configurations and the metric used for distance calculation (Hamming distance).
paper_structure: The paper develops diagnostics (BID and network analysis) to probe the ergodicity-breaking transition in the quantum sun model, showing how these metrics yield distinct signatures for the ergodic, critical, and nonergodic phases.
why_interesting: It provides novel, experimentally accessible, data-driven signatures (BID, network topology) to diagnose fundamental quantum phenomena like ergodicity breaking, bridging quantum dynamics with modern data science tools.
